headline: Ecosia, the Berlin search engine, is dropping Mistral as its AI supplier for open models, some of them Chinese, its chief executive told POLITICO.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the interview was published 6 Oct, before the window; the 8 Oct pieces relay it.
importance_line: It is a visible customer loss for Europe's best-known AI company and a sign that firms wanting top open models may end up using Chinese ones, but the quality and cost claims come from Ecosia's chief executive and Mistral did not answer POLITICO's request for comment.
summary: POLITICO Europe reported on 6 Oct 2026, from an interview with Ecosia chief executive Christian Kroll, that the search engine is replacing Mistral, the French AI company it adopted in May, because he finds its models about a year behind, its servers kept overloading and its foreign investors undermine its claim to be sovereign; PPC Land and Trending Topics relayed the story. Ecosia now uses open-weight models (ones whose trained settings are published for anyone to download), including China's Qwen, GLM and Kimi, hosted through the German platform Melious, and Kroll says this roughly halved costs, a figure that is his own.
notes: POLITICO's page and Cybernews blocked (403); text read through PPC Land and Trending Topics. URL is POLITICO's link as decoded from Google News.
